rows.stem:
A block slides down a rough incline at angle theta = 30 degrees above the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is 0.20. The block is modeled as a point (a dot).

Write the item ID HDG-2026-PHYS1-001 at the top of your page. Draw a complete free-body diagram of the block, showing every force acting on it while it slides down.
rows.capture_instruction: Draw one free-body diagram on one page. Write only the item ID at the top of the page, then photograph the full page with all diagram evidence visible.
rows.canonical_answer: Three individual force vectors, each drawn as a straight arrow originating on the dot: (1) gravity (weight, Fg = mg) pointing straight down; (2) the normal force (Fn) pointing perpendicular to and away from the incline surface; (3) the kinetic friction force (Ff) acting along the incline surface, pointing up the incline (opposing the block's down-the-incline sliding motion). No net-force vector and no component (x/y-resolved) vectors should be drawn -- only the three individual forces, each labeled.

expected_graph_spec.representation: free-body diagram: point (dot) with individual straight-line force-vector arrows
accepted_variants: vector lengths are not graded for exact scale -- only presence, direction, and correct originating point matter

criterion_definitions.met_rule: Every force is drawn as a straight arrow that originates on the dot and points away from it (not resolved into components, not double-headed).
A force vector labeled gravity/weight/Fg/mg points straight down from the dot.
A force vector labeled normal/Fn points away from and perpendicular to the incline surface (not straight up).
A force vector labeled friction/Ff points up along the incline surface, opposing the block's down-the-incline motion.
No net-force vector, no gravity-component vectors, and no other forces (e.g. an unspecified applied force) are drawn -- exactly the three forces above.
Each of the three vectors is labeled with a name or symbol identifying which force it represents.

rows.notes: New hand-drawn capture item authored 2026-08-18 to close the Physics hand-drawn coverage gap identified in HAND_DRAWN_RESPONSE_MIX_AUDIT_2026_08_18.md. Free-body-diagram convention (arrows originate on the dot, forces in the same direction drawn side by side, individual forces not net force) taken directly from the vector-diagram convention documented in AP_PHYSICS_1_CED_FACT_PACK.md / AP_PHYSICS_2_CED_FACT_PACK.md, confirmed as a standing Physics 1/2/C-family rule, not unit-specific. Scenario numbers are illustrative (not used in grading criteria, which are direction/presence-only) and were not cross-checked against a released FRQ this session. Do not expose criterion definitions to the person drawing the diagram.

rows.stem:
A ball is thrown straight up from the ground with an initial speed of 20 m/s. Take up as the positive direction and use g = 10 m/s^2. The ball returns to the ground 4.0 s after it is thrown.

Write the item ID HDG-2026-PHYS1-002 at the top of your page. Sketch the velocity-vs-time graph of the ball from t = 0 s to t = 4.0 s.
rows.capture_instruction: Draw one graph on one page. Write only the item ID at the top of the page, then photograph the full page with all graph evidence visible.
rows.canonical_answer: A single straight line with constant negative slope (-10 m/s^2, i.e. -g) throughout the entire interval, since the only acceleration is gravity, both while rising and while falling. The line starts at v = +20 m/s at t = 0 s, crosses v = 0 at t = 2.0 s (the peak of the ball's flight), and reaches v = -20 m/s at t = 4.0 s (just before landing). No kink, curve, or change of slope occurs at t = 2.0 s -- only the sign of v changes, not the slope.

expected_graph_spec.representation: single straight line, velocity (m/s) vs. time (s)
expected_graph_spec.y_axis: velocity (m/s), roughly -20 to +20, with up as positive
accepted_variants: exact numeric slope/points are not required to be plotted to scale, but the straight-line shape, sign of the intercepts, and the zero-crossing at t = 2.0 s must be shown

criterion_definitions.met_rule: X-axis labeled time (s) spanning at least 0-4; Y-axis labeled velocity (m/s), with the positive direction (up) noted or implied by a labeled positive intercept.
The entire graph is one straight line with constant slope -- no curvature and no change of slope anywhere on the interval.
The line starts at v = +20 m/s (or a value recognizably close to it) at t = 0.
The line crosses v = 0 at t = 2.0 s, marking the top of the flight.
The line reaches v = -20 m/s (or a value recognizably close to it) at t = 4.0 s.
The slope is negative and unchanged across the entire interval, including through the v = 0 crossing (no flattening or kink at the peak).

rows.notes: New hand-drawn capture item authored 2026-08-18, same batch as HDG-2026-PHYS1-001. Directly exercises the graphical-relationships skill named in AP_PHYSICS_1_CED_FACT_PACK.md (instantaneous velocity = slope of position-time graph; students expected to sketch appropriate graphs from qualitative/quantitative motion descriptions). Kinematics numbers are simple, exact, and independently verifiable (v = v0 - g t); not cross-checked against a released FRQ this session. Do not expose criterion definitions to the person drawing the graph.
